title: northwatch-scratchpad-mira-2027-01-11
content:
First watch scratchpad — Mira (concise log for followups)
Date: 2027-01-11 (night shift)
Shift summary: 00:45-08:15 PST. Two small pages: 01:12 (redis cache flapping), 03:50 (high 5xx rate for hosted-api-us-west). Both resolved with fallbacks; need followups.

01) Redis cache flapping (01:12) - Symptoms: sudden spike in redis connection errors from serving runtime pools A/B. Errors surfaced as transient KV cache misses + timeout to redis replica. Error sample: "ERR Connection timed out" in logs.
- Immediate mitigation: scaled serving-runtime pool A from 6 -> 10 replicas (manual scale), routed traffic to pool B; applied temporary routing rule to reduce prefilling.
- Root-cause hypothesis: redis replica maintenance (automatic failover) overlapped with backup snapshot job (cron 01:00). Replica entered election, primaries stayed up but connections dropped.
- Runbook TODOs:
  * Add note for "redis maintenance window" to infra-runbook: include snapshot job timing and warn against scheduling during failover windows.
  * Add automated detection to alert when >3% of KV ops return connection errors in 5m window (SRE-4821).
  * Create a canary for serving-runtime reconnect logic: if reconnect loop triggers > N times within 2m, escalate to ops channel instead of relying on auto-retry.
- Follow-ups: open infra ticket to shift snapshot from 01:00 -> 03:00 in staging only (low risk) and verify with infra team. Assigned: Jordan. ETA: 2027-01-14.

02) Hosted API 5xx spike (03:50) - Symptoms: Elevated 5xx across several endpoints: /v1/generate (p95 latency up), internal traces show model worker OOMs on dedicated quantized instance type.
- Immediate mitigation: Activate fallback routing to model-variant: gptq-1.5-small for low-priority tenants; throttled long-running requests; restarted model-worker on host infra-rt-07.
- Quick command snippets I ran (save for runbook):
  * kubectl -n serving get pods -o wide | grep infra-rt-07
  * kubectl -n serving logs model-worker-rt-07 -c runtime | sed -n '1,200p'
  * sudo journalctl -u nvidia-runtime --since "3 hours ago" | grep -i oom
- Root-cause hypothesis: model-worker memory pressure caused by unexpected large prompt with streaming enabled + prefilling disabled; combination triggered aggressive KV cache retention and forced heavy attention matrices.
- Runbook TODOs:
  * Add a checklist for "model worker OOM triage": collect container logs, dmesg, kcaches, last successful checkpoint.
  * Add a short-circuit fallback in routing policy to degrade to low-memory model-variants when OOM probability modeled > 0.6.
  * Instrument request meter to log "prompt-token-count" and flag when > 16k tokens incoming.
- Follow-ups: Create PR for routing policy change (infra PR linked in artifacts). Owner: Samir. ETA: 2027-01-18.

03) Post-incident small tasks (low effort)
- Update night-shift checklist: add steps to check redis replica health page and model-worker memstats.
- Add a pointer in our Slack #ops-channel pinned messages to the new temporary routing command we used.
- Draft a short incident note (one-paragraph) for CS so they can notify affected customers (low priority tenants only).

04) Open questions / scribbles
- Should we increase the cold-cache threshold for fallback routing? pros/cons quick list:
  * pros: fewer OOMs, predictable latency at cost of increased tokens on cheaper models.
  * cons: potential quality regressions for tenants relying on larger variants.
- Can we add a short flag to telemetry that marks a request as "prefill=true/false" so we can split metrics?
- Is there a way to sandbox snapshot cron so it does not touch replica nodes during leader election? (ask infra)

05) Paging notes (for next handoff)
- What to watch for: rise in redis connection error rate (>0.5% baseline) or model-worker OOMs repeated more than twice in 1h.
- Quick mitigation commands:
  * reroute: /infra/routing toggle --from=poolA --to=poolB --reason="redis-failover"
  * scale: kubectl -n serving scale statefulset serving-runtime --replicas=10
  * restart model-worker: kubectl -n serving rollout restart deployment/model-worker-rt-07
- Contacts: Jordan Lee (infra lead), Samir Gupta (runtime), Priya Rao (customer liaison)

6) Retro bullets (for 1pager/weekly)
- Automation gap: snapshot timing + failover coordination.
- Observability gap: need metric for "KV connection error rate" and prompt-size telemetry.
- Ops ergonomics: make fallback routing as simple as a single CLI command and attach to runbook.

7) Misc notes to self
- Remember to add sample log snippets to the runbook (truncate long traces).
- Keep the temporary routing rule ID somewhere searchable (used id: route-2027-0111-01).
- If we touch the routing policy, add a TTL so it automatically expires after 6h unless extended.

End of scratchpad. Will convert bite-sized items into tickets tomorrow (Jordan/Samir owners noted).

Raw log snippets (copied into ticket drafts):
"2027-01-11T01:12:23Z coredriver[serving-runtime] ERROR kv_conn timeout peer 10.12.4.21"
"2027-01-11T03:51:04Z model-worker-rt-07 OOMKilled: runtime matrix allocate 24.3GB needed"

-- Mira P.
(oncall, eng-sre)
